newsitem.title: PERU: Profit-taking pushes Lima bolsa to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking pushes Lima bolsa to lower close.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed a notch lower Thursday, as investors took gains from recent bull runs, and traders expected investors to extend profit-taking in coming days before jumping back into the market.
"It's a small healthy drop after consecutive rises. Only stocks in mining company Morococha resisted well," said trader Carlos Guimeth, at Multivalores brokerage.

The blue-chip index closed down 0.38 percent at 2,708.83 points, while the general index ended down 0.39 percent to 1,851.72 points, according to preliminary figures at the market's 1330 local time (1830 GMT) close.
The main blue-chip loser was miner Atacocha , which fell 5.03 percent to close at 1.70 soles, with a volume of 1.32 million shares traded. Traders put the drop down to profit-taking.
Morococha closed up 10.16 percent at 4.88 soles, but with a modest volume of 266,325 shares traded. Traders said the share price was now overvalued.
Morococha "has risen with interesting volumes, but its share price is now overvalued compared to the value of the company," said trader Julio Alcalde at brokerage MGS & Associates.
Miner Morococha has seen sharp gains in recent days on the back of U.S. Phelps Dodge's announcement that it had bought a 27 percent stake in the mining company, traders said.
Its recent gains have also benefited from firm world zinc price.
Elsewhere blue-chip heavyweight Telefonica del Peru closed down 1.07 percent at 6.48 soles, with 1.06 million shares traded.
Electricity firm Edegel, with a heavy 2.2 million shares traded, closed down 2.19 percent at 1.34 soles, due to profit-taking.
